chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"I do not see it for a man to swear except by Allah, the Exalted." And he said, "The man's saying when he says: 'No, by your enemy' is indeed from the speech of Ignorance. If people were to swear by this and similar phrases, swearing by Allah would be abandoned."

key_terms.بِالشَّانِئَةِ: by the enemy (commonly used in oaths)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on swearing by 'your enemy' and why is it discouraged?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the exclusivity of swearing by Allah, critiquing the pre-Islamic custom of invoking 'your enemy' (shani'aka) as a sign of Jahiliyyah. He warns that the proliferation of such alternative oaths risks marginalizing the divine name, thereby diminishing the spiritual gravity of the oath in communal practice.
